summary: The narrator, recovering in LA after the confrontation with Pithica, has lost odd-job work and drinks heavily while alone with his thoughts about Dawna, Pithica, and Rio. A report from Checker says over seventy percent of Pithica's revenue sources moved their money out of the organization's reach. After a vivid, disturbing dream, the narrator punches a wall and then fixates on the word "Halberd," which he associates with a memo Anton once gave him.
one_line: A battered narrator drinks alone in post-disaster LA, haunted by Pithica, Dawna, and a nagging memory of the word "Halberd."
key_facts: The narrator's odd jobs in LA dried up by the second week after the disaster because people were no longer desperate enough to hire him for necessities.
Arthur had gone back to his own place, leaving the narrator alone with his thoughts.
A week and a half after the final confrontation with Pithica, Checker emailed the narrator saying he had been keeping tabs.
According to Checker, over seventy percent of Pithica's revenue sources had moved their money out of the organization's reach.
Dawna and her people would need a long time to rebuild Pithica's resources.
The narrator's nightmares had been worse in the past couple of weeks, since Dawna.
The narrator punched his fist through the drywall next to the mattress, bloodying his knuckles.
The narrator picked up a bottle with a stylized drawing of an axe on its label and kept thinking of the word "Halberd."
The word "Halberd" reminded the narrator of a memo that Anton had given him a lifetime ago, which mentioned Halberd and Pithica.
The narrator experiences a strong sense of déjà vu and feels he has seen or dreamt the images from his dream before.
